# Setup & Component Choice

## Installation

```bash
npm install @kritzel/vue-editor
```

`@kritzel/vue-editor` wraps the core `@kritzel/engine` web components in typed Vue 3 components (generated by the Stencil Vue output target) and re-exports all classes/types you need â€” import everything from `@kritzel/vue-editor`, or from `@kritzel/engine` when intentionally building an engine-only integration.

There is **no app-level setup**: no plugin, no `app.use()`, no `defineCustomElements` call. Rendering `<KritzelEditor>` registers the custom elements automatically.

## Global sizing CSS

The editor fills its host; the host must have a concrete size. For a full-page canvas:

```css
/* styles.css */
html, body, #app {
  width: 100dvw;
  height: 100dvh;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
  overflow: hidden;
}
```

```html
<KritzelEditor style="display: block; width: 100%; height: 100%" />
```

In a flex-column layout (toolbar above the canvas), size the editor with `:style="{ flex: 1, minHeight: 0, display: 'block' }"`.

For mobile, add to `index.html`:

```html
<meta name="viewport" content="viewport-fit=cover, width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=no, maximum-scale=1.0, minimum-scale=1.0, interactive-widget=resizes-content" />
```

## Editor vs. Engine â€” decision rule

| | `<KritzelEditor>` | `<KritzelEngine>` |
|---|---|---|
| Toolbar, settings, workspace manager, export UI | âœ… built in (each part hideable) | âŒ none |
| Tools registered by default | âœ… selection, brush, eraser, line, shape, text, image | âŒ **none â€” you must `registerTool` yourself** |
| Readiness event | `@isReady` â†’ `CustomEvent<EditorIsReadyEvent>` | `@isEngineReady` â†’ `CustomEvent<KritzelEngineState>` |
| Native element type | `HTMLKritzelEditorElement` via `getEditorRef` | `HTMLKritzelEngineElement` via `getEngineRef` |
| Programmatic object/viewport API | âœ… full (delegates to engine) | âœ… full |
| Typical use | Default. Hide pieces via `isToolbarVisible`, `isMoreMenuVisible`, `isWorkspaceManagerVisible`, `isUtilityPanelVisible` | Fully custom UI around a bare canvas |

**Prefer hiding editor UI over dropping to the engine.** A "chrome-less" editor still gives you context menus, shortcuts and tool plumbing:

```html
<KritzelEditor
  ref="editor"
  editorId="embedded"
  :isToolbarVisible="false"
  :isMoreMenuVisible="false"
  :isWorkspaceManagerVisible="false"
  :isUtilityPanelVisible="false"
  @isReady="onReady"
  style="display: block; width: 100%; height: 100%"
/>
```

## Getting the native element (`getEditorRef` / `getEngineRef`)

A template ref on `<KritzelEditor>` points to the Vue **component instance**, not the DOM element. Use the `getEditorRef`/`getEngineRef` composables to resolve the native element: pass the template-ref **name** as a string, and you get back a computed ref to the `HTMLKritzelEditorElement`/`HTMLKritzelEngineElement`. Like `useTemplateRef`, they must be called at the **top level of `<script setup>`** â€” never inside a function or handler.

## Component skeleton (editor)

```html
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { KritzelEditor, getEditorRef, type EditorIsReadyEvent } from '@kritzel/vue-editor'

const editor = getEditorRef('editor') // computed ref to HTMLKritzelEditorElement | null
const isReady = ref(false)

async function onReady(event: Event) {
  const detail = (event as CustomEvent<EditorIsReadyEvent>).detail
  isReady.value = true
  // all programmatic API usage starts here, via editor.value (every method is async)
  await editor.value?.setViewport(0, 0, 1)
}
</script>

<template>
  <KritzelEditor
    ref="editor"
    editorId="board"
    @isReady="onReady"
    style="display: block; width: 100%; height: 100vh"
  />
</template>
```

Event handlers receive a plain DOM `Event`; cast to `CustomEvent<T>` to read the payload from `.detail`. `EditorIsReadyEvent` contains `host`, `activeWorkspace` (`id`, `name`, `isPublic`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`), `syncConfig`, `assetStorageConfig`, `loginConfig`, and `theme`.

## Headless engine skeleton

The engine registers **no tools** â€” without registration the canvas accepts no input. Register at least a selection or brush tool in the `@isEngineReady` handler:

```html
<script setup lang="ts">
import {
  KritzelEngine, KritzelBrushTool, KritzelEraserTool, KritzelSelectionTool,
  getEngineRef,
} from '@kritzel/vue-editor'

const engine = getEngineRef('engine') // computed ref to HTMLKritzelEngineElement | null

async function onReady() {
  if (!engine.value) return
  await engine.value.registerTool('selection', KritzelSelectionTool)
  await engine.value.registerTool('brush', KritzelBrushTool)
  await engine.value.registerTool('eraser', KritzelEraserTool)
  await engine.value.changeActiveTool('brush')
}
</script>

<template>
  <KritzelEngine
    ref="engine"
    editorId="headless"
    @isEngineReady="onReady"
    style="display: block; width: 100%; height: 100%"
  />
</template>
```

Engine-only extras: it additionally exposes `exportAsJson`, `importFromJson`, `getIsPublic`, `saveSettings`, `loadSettings`, and the `workspace` prop. Editor-only extras: `toolbar`, `customSvgIcons`, `loginConfig`, UI visibility flags, `openLoginDialog`, `setLoginLoading`.

## Prop stability (the Vue-specific rule)

The wrapper assigns object/array props to the underlying web component **by reference, whenever identity changes**. An inline object literal in the template (`:syncConfig="{ providers: [...] }"`) is recreated on every render, re-runs the component's prop setters, and can reset internal state. Therefore:

- Define object/array props (`toolbar`, `syncConfig`, `themes`, theme objects, context-menu arrays) as **consts in `<script setup>`** (created once per component instance) or at module scope for shared static config.
- Inside context-menu actions and control callbacks, access the editor via `editor.value?.` â€” the computed ref from `getEditorRef` is identity-stable.

```html
<script setup lang="ts">
import { KritzelEditor, IndexedDBSyncProvider, type KritzelSyncConfig } from '@kritzel/vue-editor'

const syncConfig: KritzelSyncConfig = { providers: [IndexedDBSyncProvider] }
</script>

<template>
  <KritzelEditor :syncConfig="syncConfig" style="display: block; width: 100%; height: 100vh" />
</template>
```

## Multiple instances

Every concurrently mounted editor/engine needs a unique `editorId` â€” it namespaces settings (localStorage) and persistence (IndexedDB) keys. Without it, instances clobber each other's stored state.

```html
<KritzelEditor editorId="left-board" ... />
<KritzelEditor editorId="right-board" ... />
```

## Common setup mistakes

- Canvas invisible â†’ host element has no size (rule: explicit `display: block` + width/height, or `flex: 1; min-height: 0`).
- "Method X failed / editor.value is null" â†’ called before `@isReady`/`@isEngineReady` fired, or the string passed to `getEditorRef`/`getEngineRef` doesn't match the `ref` name in the template, or the composable was called outside the top level of `<script setup>`.
- Headless engine ignores all pointer input â†’ no tools registered.
- Two boards share drawings/settings â†’ missing distinct `editorId`.
- Editor resets/re-initializes when surrounding UI state changes â†’ object/array props (`syncConfig`, `toolbar`, `themes`, menus) written as inline literals in the template; hoist them into `<script setup>` consts.
